# logfire_dashboard (Resource)

Manages a Logfire dashboard.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "logfire_project" "example" {
  name = "example-project"
}

resource "logfire_dashboard" "example" {
  project_id = logfire_project.example.id
  name       = "example-dashboard"
  slug       = "example-dashboard"
  definition = file("${path.module}/dashboard.json")
}
```

Use `file()` to read a dashboard definition written by hand or copied from Logfire.
Exported metadata can remain unchanged; `project_id`, `name`, and `slug` select the
destination and identity.

| Starting point | Terraform workflow |
| --- | --- |
| Defined in IaC | Apply the definition to create a dashboard. |
| Existing UI dashboard | Export its JSON, match its attributes, and import before applying to retain its UUID. |
| Copy of a UI dashboard | Apply its exported JSON with the destination project, name, and an available slug to create a new UUID. The source dashboard remains unchanged. |

## Definition comparison

Comparison ignores JSON formatting, top-level `metadata`, known defaults,
and grid panel `ref` and `$ref` aliases. Integer literals compare exactly.
Decimal and exponent literals compare at the API's float precision. Equivalent
spellings such as `1` and `1.0` compare equal. Content and layout changes produce
a plan.

The resource's `name` and `slug` control the dashboard name and URL. Changing
`name`, `definition`, or `allow_ui_edits` updates the dashboard. Changing
`project_id` or `slug` replaces it.

Definition updates explicitly request the file's layout, including panel visibility.
Name-only updates preserve saved UI positions. On older instances without layout
replacement support, saved UI overrides can cause an inconsistent result error
when applying a layout change. Re-export the dashboard to adopt its current layout.

## Managed dashboards

Every create and update marks the dashboard as managed by Terraform. Logfire
shows a "Managed by Terraform" badge on the dashboard. It refuses edits from its
UI, MCP server, and Assistant, because the next apply overwrites them. Set
`allow_ui_edits = true` to keep the badge and allow those edits.

The provider does not read the mark back, so it never appears in a plan. A
Logfire instance without managed dashboard support saves the dashboard and
ignores the mark.

After an upgrade from a provider version without `allow_ui_edits`, the first plan
shows an in-place update of each dashboard that sets `allow_ui_edits`. That
update applies the mark. An imported dashboard gets the mark on its first update.
The mark stays on a dashboard that leaves the Terraform state without a destroy.

A tool that wraps this provider names itself in the `LOGFIRE_MANAGED_BY`
environment variable of the provider process. The accepted values are
`terraform` (the default), `pulumi`, and any other name of at most 64
characters. Do not set it for Terraform or OpenTofu.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `definition` (String) Dashboard definition JSON payload.
- `name` (String) Dashboard display name.
- `project_id` (String) Project UUID used for API paths.
- `slug` (String) Dashboard slug used in URLs.

### Optional

- `allow_ui_edits` (Boolean) Whether Logfire users can edit the dashboard. Logfire marks the dashboard as managed by this tool and refuses edits from its UI, MCP server, and Assistant. Set to `true` to keep the mark and allow those edits. The next apply overwrites them. Defaults to `false`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Dashboard UUID assigned by the backend.

## Import

Set `project_id`, `name`, and `slug` to the existing dashboard's values and save
its exported JSON to `dashboard.json`. Import by project name and dashboard slug:

```terraform
import {
  to = logfire_dashboard.example
  id = "example-project/example-dashboard"
}
```

Or use the command line:

```shell
terraform import logfire_dashboard.example "example-project/example-dashboard"
terraform plan -detailed-exitcode
```

With a matching export and configuration, the first plan reports no changes and
exits with code `0`. Import adopts the existing dashboard UUID.

Import also accepts `project_uuid/dashboard_uuid`, with an optional third
component for the slug. Commas and pipes are accepted instead of slashes.
